name: dwarf

attributes.attribute: not true dwarves but small versions of normal humans

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: A dwarf is a folkloric figure of small stature. Dwarfs are little people. They appear in most Celtic lands. They were immigrants from Scandinavia or Germany. There they were common folkloric characters who resembled trolls. In Irish lore a dwarf was either a fairy or a small person. The harpist of Fionn Mac Cumhaill, Cnú Deiréil, was a small person. The fairy dwarves were not true dwarves. They were shapely small versions of normal humans. Legends of small people inspired one great English satire. Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels. Its human hero was a giant among the small Lilliputians.

okr.objective: Define dwarves as folkloric figures of small size and trace their origin to Scandinavia or Germany.
key_results: State that dwarves are little people who came to Celtic lands
Sort Irish dwarves as fairies or small persons like Cnú Deiréil
Link dwarf legends to the satire of Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels
